issue_paraphrase: A Set-Cookie header whose Expires attribute contains non-ASCII digits (for example Arabic-Indic or fullwidth numerals) is accepted as a valid expiry timestamp, even though RFC 6265 requires the date to be pure ASCII. aiohttp parses the malformed value into a concrete expiration time and stores the cookie with that expiry instead of rejecting the date and treating the cookie as a session cookie.
fix_summary: Added re.ASCII to the five DATE_*_RE regexes in aiohttp/cookiejar.py so \d, \w-style token and month matching only accept ASCII, making _parse_date return None for non-ASCII digits per RFC 6265 section 5.1.1.
notes: Pure-Python code path, no event loop, no network, runs in <0.1s. Install built with AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS=1 (pure-Python build; skips Cython/llhttp compile); cookiejar has no C counterpart so the bug is identical in the accelerated build. Python 3.12.13 on bench-base:python-3.12. pytest config in setup.cfg turns warnings into errors and sets per-test timeout=120 via pytest-timeout (both plugins installed).

issue_paraphrase: Reading request.forwarded on an inbound request hangs indefinitely when the Forwarded header ends with an empty or malformed element, such as 'Forwarded: ; a' or a bare trailing name without '='. The parsing loop fails to advance and spins forever, stalling the single-threaded event loop on which it runs, so one hostile header value can wedge any handler that touches request.forwarded.
fix_summary: In the forwarded header parser inside BaseRequest.forwarded, compute the next ';' once (semi := field_value.find(';', pos)); if there is none, break out of the loop instead of slicing field_value[pos:-1] and re-assigning a position that can wrap around and loop forever.
notes: Pure-Python property on web_request; repro hangs rather than raising, so always run the failing direction under a shell timeout or pytest-timeout (setup.cfg sets per-test timeout=120). No network, no event loop beyond make_mocked_request. Verification took <1s at fix, bounded by timeout at parent. Test file tests/test_web_request.py contains many other tests; run just the golden test by node id.

issue_paraphrase: A WebSocket peer that closes the connection with reserved status code 1006 (ABNORMAL_CLOSURE, used only internally to signal an abnormal drop) is treated as a normal close: aiohttp accepts the Close frame and reports code 1006 instead of flagging a protocol violation. The spec forbids 1006 on the wire, so the reader should raise a protocol error while still rejecting the other reserved codes 1004, 1005 and 1015.
fix_summary: Removed WSCloseCode.ABNORMAL_CLOSURE (1006) from ALLOWED_CLOSE_CODES in aiohttp/_websocket/reader_py.py so a received close frame with code 1006 raises WebSocketError(WSCloseCode.PROTOCOL_ERROR) like the other reserved codes. The C reader (reader_c) is cythonized from reader_py.py (see Makefile), so the same logic applies in the accelerated build after regeneration.
notes: Verified in the pure-Python build (AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS=1) where reader_py is used directly; the test file imports aiohttp._websocket.reader_py explicitly, so it is deterministic. No network, <1s. The parser fixture wires a full WSReader; tests are sync (no asyncio). setup.cfg turns warnings into errors; pytest-timeout/pytest-aiohttp/pytest-asyncio/freezegun/coverage must be installed or conftest errors out.
